title: Source Hom is the product colimit of numerators
statement: Let $C,D,E$ be categories, $W,W^{\prime}$ morphism properties on $C,D$, assume $W^{\prime}$ has a right calculus of fractions, and let $Q:D\to E$ be a localization at $W^{\prime}$. Fix a functor $F:C\to D$ and objects $K\in C,M\in D,V\in E$. Let $J,T,H$ be the denominator categories and numerator diagram [def-pc-derived-adjunction-hom-diagram], and let $R:J\to E$ send $s:K\to I$ to $QF(I)$. Assume $R$ is essentially constant with value $V$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram]. For every cocone $p:R\to V$ satisfying the chosen splitting and factorization clauses of that definition, there exists a bijective map $\phi:H.\mathrm{ColimitType}\to\operatorname{Hom}_E(QM,V)$ whose value at each representative $(s,t,f)$ is $Q(t)^{-1}Q(f)p_s$ in diagrammatic composition. No adjunction or pro value is assumed.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 0FND proof, first three equalities; Stacks Tag 0FND (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FND)

proof.text: Define the cocone on H by inverse incoming denominator, localized numerator and p_s. An incoming triangle preserves its right fraction, and an outgoing triangle commutes with p, so the cocone descends to ColimitType.
For any h:Q(M)→V choose the section a:V→R(s₀) from the chosen splitting. Represent h followed by a as a right fraction. Its image in the cocone is h, by a followed by p_s₀ = identity.

For two representatives with equal images, apply the factorization clause at each outgoing stage. Use IsFilteredOrEmpty.cocone_objs to join the resulting stages and cocone_maps to coequalize their arrows from s₀. The resulting transitions both factor through p, a, and the same map from s₀. Postcomposing the assumed equality therefore equates the transported right fractions.

Apply the common-refinement criterion to these right fractions. The resulting incoming triangles have equal transported numerators at the common outgoing stage. Functor.ιColimitType_eq_of_map_eq_map identifies the two original representatives; this proves injectivity.

lean.statement: theorem derivedAdjunction_source_colimit {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] {E : Type uE} [Category.{vE} E] (W : MorphismProperty C) (W' : MorphismProperty D) [W'.HasRightCalculusOfFractions] (Q : D ⥤ E) [Q.IsLocalization W'] (F : C ⥤ D) (K : C) (M : D) (V : E) : let R := MorphismProperty.Under.forget W ⊤ K ⋙ Under.forget K ⋙ F ⋙ Q IsEssentiallyConstantIndDiagram R V → ∀ p : R ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj V, (∃ (s₀ : W.Under ⊤ K) (a : V ⟶ R.obj s₀), a ≫ p.app s₀ = 𝟙 V ∧ ∀ s, ∃ (s₁ : W.Under ⊤ K) (b : s₀ ⟶ s₁) (c : s ⟶ s₁), R.map c = p.app s ≫ a ≫ R.map b) → ∃ φ : (derivedAdjunctionHomDiagram W W' F K M).ColimitType → (Q.obj M ⟶ V), Function.Bijective φ ∧ ∀ (s : W.Under ⊤ K) (t : W'.Over ⊤ M) (f : t.left ⟶ F.obj s.right), φ ((derivedAdjunctionHomDiagram W W' F K M).ιColimitType (s, Opposite.op t) f) = (MorphismProperty.RightFraction.mk t.hom t.prop f).map Q (Localization.inverts Q W') ≫ p.app s
